title: Solving Floor and Ceiling Equations Equal to Zero
originalTopic: The Greatest and Least Integer Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine all real values of x for which (a) floor(x) = 0 and (b) ceiling(x) = 0.

steps.title: Recall the Definition of the Floor Function for Part (a)
steps.explanation: The greatest integer function floor(x) denotes the largest integer less than or equal to x. Setting n = 0 gives the exact condition for floor(x) = 0.
steps.why: An integer n is the greatest integer <= x if and only if n <= x < n + 1.

steps.title: Solve floor(x) = 0
steps.explanation: Every real number in [0, 1) is at least 0 and strictly less than 1, so its greatest integer is 0.
steps.why: Numbers below 0 have floor <= -1, and numbers >= 1 have floor >= 1.

steps.title: Recall the Ceiling Definition and Solve ceiling(x) = 0 for Part (b)
steps.mathExpression: \lceil x \rceil = n \iff n - 1 < x \le n \implies \lceil x \rceil = 0 \iff -1 < x \le 0
steps.explanation: The least integer function ceiling(x) denotes the smallest integer greater than or equal to x. Setting n = 0 gives -1 < x <= 0, or (-1, 0].
steps.why: An integer n is the least integer >= x if and only if n - 1 < x <= n.
